I am 60 years old, and I have farmed these fields in Quzhou County my whole life. My father taught me, and I have seen what works on this flat land of the North China Plain. I have eight mu of good irrigated land. I will not gamble with strange crops or new techniques I do not trust.

This year, I will stick to the **winter wheat–summer maize rotation** on all eight mu. That is what the machinery, the markets, and my experience are built for. I sowed the wheat last October, and now that the frost is breaking, the growing season is truly beginning.

**For the winter wheat:** I planted *Jimai 22*, an improved variety I know well. It is hardy and the grain station pays a fair price for it. I will apply about 30 kg of nitrogen per mu—half as compound fertilizer broadcast before green-up, and half as urea topdressed at the jointing stage. I will also put down 12 kg of phosphorus and 8 kg of potassium per mu to keep the soil from wearing out. I will irrigate four times: the winter irrigation is already done, and now I will water at green-return, heading, and grain-filling. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice. I till with the rotary tiller in spring to break the crust and let the fertilizer in. I expect about 1,000 kg per mu.

**For the summer maize:** As soon as the wheat comes off the combine in early June, I will plant *Denghai 605*, a hybrid seed with good drought tolerance. I will not till again—no-tillage saves time, fuel, and moisture, and the wheat stubble protects the young maize from the hot winds of July. I will apply about 25 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu at sowing and jointing. I will irrigate twice: right after sowing and again at the big trumpet stage. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice to control the bollworm. I expect about 1,100 kg per mu.

I do not grow cotton anymore. The labor is too much for my back, and the price jumps around too much. Wheat and maize give me steady grain for my family and predictable cash from the buyers who come right to the village.
